arxiv-2102-00089.title: Stimuli-Sensitive Hawkes Processes for Personalized Student Procrastination Modeling Conference: Web Confernce 2021; ;
arxiv-2102-00089.creator: Mengfan Yao, Siqian Zhao, Shaghayegh Sahebi, Reza Feyzi Behnagh
arxiv-2102-00089.description: Abstract . Student procrastination and cramming for deadlines are major challenges in online learning environments, with negative educational and well-being side effects. Modeling student activities in continuous time and predicting their next study time are important problems that can help in creating personalized timely interventions to mitigate these challenges.

arxiv-2111-04720.title: Long-ranged order and flow alignment in sheared p − p- atic liquid crystals
arxiv-2111-04720.creator: Luca Giomi, John Toner, Niladri Sarkar
arxiv-2111-04720.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Luca Giomi, John Toner, Niladri Sarkar. We formulate a hydrodynamic theory of p − p- atic liquid crystals, namely two-dimensional anisotropic fluids endowed with generic p − p- fold rotational symmetry. Our approach, based on an order parameter tensor that directly embodies the discrete rotational symmetry of p − p- atic phases, allows us to unveil several unknown aspects of flowing p − p- atics, that previous theories, characterized by O ⁡ ( 2 ) {\rm O(2)} rotational symmetry, could not account for.

arxiv-2112-06307.title: Image-to-Height Domain Translation for Synthetic Aperture Sonar
arxiv-2112-06307.creator: Dylan Stewart, Shawn F. Johnson, and Alina Zare
arxiv-2112-06307.description: Abstract Observations of seabed texture with synthetic aperture sonar are dependent upon several factors. In this work, we focus on collection geometry with respect to isotropic and anisotropic textures. The low grazing angle of the collection geometry, combined with orientation of the sonar path relative to anisotropic texture, poses a significant challenge for image-alignment and other multi-view scene understanding frameworks.

arxiv-2304-07130.title: OPI at SemEval 2023 Task 9: A Simple But Effective Approach to Multilingual Tweet Intimacy Analysis
arxiv-2304-07130.creator: Sławomir Dadas
arxiv-2304-07130.description: Abstract This paper describes our submission to the SemEval 2023 multilingual tweet intimacy analysis shared task. The goal of the task was to assess the level of intimacy of Twitter posts in ten languages. The proposed approach consists of several steps. First, we perform in-domain pre-training to create a language model adapted to Twitter data.

arxiv-2305-10504.title: Model-Free Robust Average-Reward Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2305-10504.creator: Yue Wang, Alvaro Velasquez, George Atia, Ashley Prater-Bennette, Shaofeng Zou
arxiv-2305-10504.description: Abstract Robust Markov decision processes (MDPs) address the challenge of model uncertainty by optimizing the worst-case performance over an uncertainty set of MDPs. In this paper, we focus on the robust average-reward MDPs under the model-free setting. We first theoretically characterize the structure of solutions to the robust average-reward Bellman equation, which is essential for our later convergence analysis.

arxiv-2306-00245.title: From Pixels to UI Actions: Learning to Follow Instructions via Graphical User Interfaces
arxiv-2306-00245.creator: Peter Shaw, Mandar Joshi, James Cohan, Jonathan Berant, Panupong Pasupat, Hexiang Hu, Urvashi Khandelwal, Kenton Lee, Kristina Toutanova
arxiv-2306-00245.description: Abstract Much of the previous work towards digital agents for graphical user interfaces (GUIs) has relied on text-based representations (derived from HTML or other structured data sources), which are not always readily available. These input representations have been often coupled with custom, task-specific action spaces.

arxiv-2307-02570.title: Named Entity Inclusion in Abstractive Text Summarization
arxiv-2307-02570.creator: Sergey Berezin, Tatiana Batura
arxiv-2307-02570.description: Abstract We address the named entity omission - the drawback of many current abstractive text summarizers. We suggest a custom pretraining objective to enhance the model’s attention on the named entities in a text. At first, the named entity recognition model RoBERTa is trained to determine named entities in the text.

arxiv-2310-07964.title: Exploration on Incidence Geometry and Sum-Product Phenomena
arxiv-2310-07964.creator: Sung-Yi Liao
arxiv-2310-07964.description: Abstract In additive combinatorics, Erdös-Szemerédi Conjecture is an important conjecture. It can be applied to many fields, such as number theory, harmonic analysis, incidence geometry, and so on. Additionally, its statement is quite easy to understand, while it is still an open problem.

arxiv-2402-02756.title: Heterogeneous Solvent Dissipation Coupled with Particle Rearrangement in Shear Thinning Non-Brownian Suspensions
arxiv-2402-02756.creator: Tomoharu Terayama, Akira Furukawa
arxiv-2402-02756.description: Abstract Dense non-Brownian suspensions exhibit significant shear thinning, although a comprehensive understanding of the full scope of this phenomenon remains elusive. This study numerically reveals intimate heterogenous coupled dynamics between many-body particle motions and solvent hydrodynamics in shear-thinning non-Brownian suspensions.

arxiv-2402-04040.title: Status of R-parity violating SUSY
arxiv-2402-04040.creator: Arghya Choudhury, Arpita Mondal, and Subhadeep Mondal
arxiv-2402-04040.description: Abstract In this article, we discuss various phenomenological implications of possible R-parity violating (RPV) supersymmetric scenarios. In this context, the implications of both bilinear and trilinear RPV terms are reviewed from the viewpoint of neutrino physics, anomalous muon magnetic moment, different flavor observables, and collider physics.

arxiv-2403-10185.title: Can Factual Statements be Deceptive? The DeFaBel Corpus of Belief-based Deception
arxiv-2403-10185.description: Abstract If a person firmly believes in a non-factual statement, such as “ The Earth is flat ”, and argues in its favor, there is no inherent intention to deceive. As the argumentation stems from genuine belief, it may be unlikely to exhibit the linguistic properties associated with deception or lying.

arxiv-2504-15409.title: Magnetic recoil interferometer in a uniform gravitational field. Comment on “Observation of the quantum equivalence principle for matter-waves”
arxiv-2504-15409.creator: Peter Asenbaum 1 , Chris Overstreet 2
arxiv-2504-15409.description: Abstract The calculation of the phase shift of a matter-wave interferometer looks different for different coordinate choices or the addition of a uniform gravitational field, but the final result of the observable phase shift does not depend on the coordinate choices or the uniform gravitational field.

arxiv-2509-22752.title: Proposal of method to solve a Traveling Salesman Problem using Variational Quantum Kolmogorov-Arnold Network
arxiv-2509-22752.creator: Hikaru Wakaura
arxiv-2509-22752.description: Abstract Traveling salesman problems (TSP) are one of the well-known combinatorial optimization problems that many groups tackle to solve. This problem appears in many types of combinational optimization, such as scheduling, route optimization, and circuit optimization. However, this problem is NP-hard, as the number of combinations increases exponentially as the number of sites increases.

arxiv-2512-04110.title: The Essentials of AI for Life and Society : A Full-Scale AI Literacy Course Accessible to All
arxiv-2512-04110.creator: Zifan Xu, Kristen Procko, Michael Munje
arxiv-2512-04110.description: Abstract In Fall 2023, we introduced a new AI Literacy class called The Essentials of AI for Life and Society (CS 109), a one-credit, seminar course consisting mainly of guest lectures, which was open to the entire university, including students, staff, and faculty.

arxiv-2601-04089.title: Tutorial on Flow-Based Network Traffic Classification Using Machine Learning
arxiv-2601-04089.creator: Adrián Pekár, Richard Plný, Karel Hynek
arxiv-2601-04089.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Adrián Pekár, Richard Plný, Karel Hynek. Modern networks carry increasingly diverse and encrypted traffic types that demand classification techniques beyond traditional port-based and payload-based methods. This tutorial provides a practical, end-to-end guide to building machine-learning-based network traffic flow classification systems. We cover the workflow from flow metering and dataset creation, through ground-truth labeling and feature engineering, to leakage-resistant experimental design, model training and evaluation, explainability, and deployment considerations.

pmc-10610166.description: luding metabolic, neurological, and age-related disorders, as well as the potential health benefits of NAD+-raising approaches. pmc-11432925.title: Effectiveness of Psychological Counseling Intervention in High-Risk Pregnancies in Italy
pmc-11432925.creator: Sofia Burgio, Gaspare Cucinella, Antonio Perino, Giovanni Baglio, Laura Crifasi, Robert Krysiak, Karolina Kowalcze, Giuseppe Gullo, Takahiro Nemoto
pmc-11432925.description: Background: The longitudinal study examines the effectiveness of a psychological support treatment for high-risk pregnancies using a between-groups design. It assesses the treatment’s impact on depression and fear of COVID-19 at three time points, and on prenatal attachment between the 20th and 24th weeks of gestation (T0), postnatal attachment 15–20 days after birth (T1), and three months after birth (T2).

pmc-11477162.title: Impact of Comorbid Polycystic Ovary Syndrome on Clinical and Laboratory Parameters in Female Adolescents with Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease: A Cross-Sectional Study
pmc-11477162.creator: Murat Keskin, Hanife Aysegul Arsoy, Ozlem Kara, Emre Sarandol, Nizameddin Koca, Yusuf Yilmaz, David E Kaplan
pmc-11477162.description: Background: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) share several pathophysiological mechanisms. While the prevalence of MASLD has been extensively studied in PCOS populations, the occurrence of PCOS among female adolescents with transient elastography (TE)-confirmed MASLD in pediatric hepatology settings remains poorly characterized.

pmc-11640412.title: Observational Analysis of Point-of-Care Lactate Plus™ Meter in Preclinical Trauma Models
pmc-11640412.creator: Catharina Gaeth, Jamila Duarte, Alvaro Rodriguez, Amber Powers, Randolph Stone, Gerald J Kost
pmc-11640412.description: Background/Objectives: Blood lactate concentration is often used to assess systemic hypoperfusion, tissue hypoxia, and sepsis in trauma patients and serves as a prognostic indicator and marker of response to therapy. Point-of-care (POC) devices provide rapid lactate measurements with a single drop of blood.

pmc-12953322.title: Comparable improvements in selective, but not sustained, attention in response to a multi-ingredient nootropic formulation when compared with caffeine
pmc-12953322.creator: Mark A. Hearris, Carl Langan-Evans, Wee-Lun Foo, Calum Garrigan, Lynn Starke, Catarina Rendeiro, Claire Williams, Philippa Jackson, James P. Morton
pmc-12953322.description: PurposeThe ergogenic effects of caffeine on cognitive performance are largely restricted to improved alertness and enhanced attention and do not typically extend to other cognitive domains. In contrast, plant extracts and phytochemicals exert broader cognitive performance benefits and, when combined together, may provide synergistic effects.

pmc-13389366.title: Bio-inspired relay catalysis for aqueous redox flow batteries
pmc-13389366.creator: Jiafeng Lei, Yaqin Zhang, Weixing Wu, Ying Wang, Jun Fan, Yi-Chun Lu
pmc-13389366.description: Aqueous redox flow batteries are promising for long-duration energy storage. However, many of them (e.g. sulfur-based and organic-based flow batteries) suffer from sluggish kinetics with low energy efficiency and insufficient capacity utilization. Here, we propose relay catalysis as a universal strategy to achieve high reaction rates while minimizing overpotential, enabling high capacity and energy efficiency.
